test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which among the following statements is NOT true about Kanishka?

options.text: He patronized Buddhist scholars Vasumitra, Asvagosha and Nagarjuna.
He convened the Fourth Buddhist Council.
Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasudeva.
The famous physician Charaka was patronized by him.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasudeva.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanishka was not succeeded by his son Vasudeva. Instead, Vasudeva I was another ruler of the Kushana dynasty who ruled after Kanishka's successors.
 
• There is no historical evidence to suggest that Kanishka was directly succeeded by Vasudeva as his son. Historical records indicate a series of rulers following Kanishka before Vasudeva came to power.
 
• Vasudeva I was the last prominent ruler of the Kushana dynasty, and his reign marked the decline of the empire.
 
• The confusion arises because Vasudeva is often associated with the late Kushana rule, but he was not a direct successor of Kanishka.
 
• Historians rely on inscriptions and coins from the era to reconstruct the succession of Kushana rulers, and these records do not support the claim that Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasudeva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kanishka's patronage of Buddhist scholars (Option 1):**

 
 
• Kanishka was a great patron of Buddhism and supported prominent Buddhist scholars such as Vasumitra, Asvaghosa, and Nagarjuna.
 
• Asvaghosa was a renowned poet and philosopher who composed "Buddhacharita," a biography of Buddha.
 
• Nagarjuna is credited with founding the Madhyamaka school of Mahayana Buddhism and made significant contributions to Buddhist philosophy.
 
• Vasumitra presided over the Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka's rule.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Buddhist Council (Option 2):**
 
 
• Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kundalvana (present-day Kashmir), which played a significant role in the development of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• The council was presided over by Vasumitra and co-chaired by Asvaghosa.
 
• It was during this council that Mahayana Buddhism was formally codified, and significant Buddhist texts were compiled and translated into Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Charaka's association with Kanishka (Option 4):**
 
 
• Charaka, the famous ancient physician and author of "Charaka Samhita," is believed to have been patronized by Kanishka.
 
• Charaka Samhita is one of the foundational texts of Ayurveda and focuses on internal medicine.
 
• Under Kanishka's patronage, Charaka made significant contributions to the field of medicine, including advancements in healthcare and surgery.
